issues.quote: The regulator on the wall had stopped.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no reading for any stopped clock or time of stopping. R1 to R4 cover only the kitchen clock, the temple, the piano and the hall clock.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the stopped regulator as a time-of-death or time-of-stopping clue, reading it as an additional clock reading that places the event at a particular moment. The sheet gives no such time.

issues.quote: His little repeater was in his hand, the one he spent four years on, and his hand was closed on it.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no reading for the repeater watch, and it says nothing about its time or its state.
issues.misreading: A repeater chimes the time on demand, so a solver could read its hour and minute as a reading the witness never gave. The closed hand adds a whereabouts or position detail the sheet does not supply.

issues.quote: Madame had said the master would come down for the toast, and I was to fetch him, as I do every year.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no time for the toast or for when the master was expected down.
issues.misreading: The reference to a toast could be read as implying a scheduled time such as midnight, which is a timing hint the sheet does not give.
